sets.title: Getters FP control: different property names across domains
sets.description: Two unrelated classes from different domains (billing vs auth) each with 8 getters, but with completely different property names. No false-positive bait here — different domains and different identifiers should not trigger token matchers.

sets.title: Getters FP probe: same property names across different domains (known_tool_fp)
sets.description: Two classes from completely different domains (billing vs logging) with identical 8 getter signatures using the same property names: id, name, email, status, createdAt, updatedAt, version, and metadata. The class bodies are otherwise unrelated implementations. This is the classic getter-chain FP bait — same property names but different domains, which legitimate token tools may incorrectly pair. Marked known_tool_fp: true as acceptable flag.

traps.reason: Deliberate FP bait: InvoiceProcessor and ActivityLogger each have 8 identical getter signatures (getId, getName, getEmail, getStatus, getCreatedAt, getUpdatedAt, getVersion, getMetadata). Token/line matchers may pair these as clones, but they are identical boilerplate ceremony from different domains — not duplicated implementation. Marked trap:false, known_tool_fp:true as acceptable flag for profiling.

Deliberate FP bait: identical getter chain to InvoiceProcessor. Same 8 getters with same property names but entirely different class implementations. A detector pairing these is reporting boilerplate similarity, not a real clone.
